coverage_note: Medi's 30:11 example (باجي + preposition) is [foreign language] in the transcript; Amal said 'two other verbs are better fit' - cannot be filed. 31:07-33:04 several [foreign language] holes (اسمعيني/اسمعلي drill). Long Latin stretches 11:47, 14:48, 20:15, 50:33-53:35. Engine: 49:38 كتبتي = خطيبتي; 05:34 بعدت = قعدت (S4); 46:48 اشرحيلي يا = اشرحيلي إياه; 50:44 في عرسه = في عرسي. Echo: 'Fee.' (17:13) = في. 48:51 Amal عزمتك likely = عزومتك (not filed). 34:47 صوت بخوف = بيخوف (S4, not filed).

rows.why: He said حلق with no owner; Amal prompted حلـ... and he rebuilt it as حلقي بوجع (my throat hurts).

rows.medi_said: would you say أرجـ- أرجعت على شغلك؟
rows.why: He used the I-form أرجعت for 'she came back'; Amal prompted هي and he said هي رجعت.

rows.chat: heyye saarat a7san u rej3at 3ala shu8ulha
rows.why: He put 'your' on work for his fiancée; Amal asked 'My work?' and he fixed it to شغلها.
rows.english: She went back to her work.

rows.why: Today (10-12) was Monday; he said Tuesday and Amal said No.

rows.medi_said: No، يوم ال-- oh، يوم الثنتين.
rows.why: He said الثنتين (two, fem) for Monday; Amal said No and he then said يوم الثنين.
Clock time needs el-; Amal said على then الـ، على الـ سبعة ونص and he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: was going to. أنا، أنا راح...
rows.amal_said: I was well. ... No، أنا كنت راح أدرس
rows.chat: ana kunet ra7 adruso, bass zabaayen aju
rows.why: For 'I was going to' he said أنا راح with no kaan; Amal prompted 'I was' and gave أنا كنت راح أدرس.
rows.english: I was going to study, but customers came.

rows.medi_said: ana, ana badzakir ul kulul, uh, aglab el فعل
rows.why: After aghlab (most of) the noun is plural (أفعال, as Amal said at 11:11); he used singular فعل and she let it pass.
rows.english: I remember most of the verbs.

rows.amal_said: This because you said بتفكري. Mm-hmm. تصحي.
rows.why: Asking Amal (a woman) he switched to the masc تصحى; she pointed out he had said بتفكري and gave تصحي.

rows.chat: shu awal ishi betfakkr fiyyo lamma tes7i
rows.why: Answering about himself he used the you-fem form بتفكري; Amal said 'I think' and بفكر.
rows.english: The first thing I think about in the morning.

rows.amal_said: About. ... فيه، فيه الصبح. You need two فيهs.
rows.chat: awal ishi ana bafakker fiyyo el-subu7
rows.why: With أول إشي fronted the verb needs فيه pointing back; Amal: 'You need two فيهs... refer it back to أول إشي'.
rows.english: The first thing I think about in the morning.

rows.chat: ahwe u shu laazem a3mal fi shu8li
rows.why: Her typed line has fi shu8li; she voiced nothing (chat alone is not a fix).
rows.english: What I have to do at my work.

rows.why: Breakfast in general takes no el-; Amal recast ما بأكل فطور.

rows.medi_said: بتِحكي an? Or would it be an, no? 'Cause it's shu.
rows.amal_said: All of the words are right, بس the order is wrong. ... we put it before what.
rows.why: He left عن at the end (and then شو عن); Amal: order is wrong, put it before what, and he said عن شو بتحكي.

rows.amal_said: بس بتفكري takes what؟ ... فيه شو بتفكري؟
rows.why: For 'thinking about' he kept عن (from talk about); Amal: بتفكري takes what? -> في.
Asked 'what are you thinking about' he said bitihki (talk); Amal named the verb بتفكري.

rows.medi_said: uh, uh, badef kee-- or do you know how... It's just badef,
rows.why: For 'do you know' he used the I-form ba3ref; Amal gave بتعرف and he said بتعرفي.
rows.english: Do you know how to play this game?

rows.why: Second verb after بتعرفي drops b-; Amal said 'No be' twice and gave تلعب.
rows.english: Do you know how to play this game?

rows.why: He used present بسمع for 'I heard'; Amal said 'I heard' and he switched to سمعت.
rows.english: I heard a scary sound outside.

rows.amal_said: This. ... ستني. ... ستنيت what does it mean؟ ... ستني is for a girl.
rows.why: He gave a past form for the fem command; Amal: -it is always past, this is a command, ستني is for a girl.

rows.amal_said: No. That's see me. ... شوفني is see me. Look at me.
rows.why: شوف is 'see'; Amal: No, that's see me - look at is بطلع على.

rows.amal_said: No. At me. ... At. تطلع علي.
rows.why: بطلع takes على; he put the object on the verb (and then -li), Amal: No. At me. تطلع علي.

rows.amal_said: No. What do I do in questions? ... In questions, what's the order of words؟
rows.why: Preposition goes in front of the question word; Amal asked about question word order and he said على شو بتطلعي.

rows.amal_said: No. Don't look. We're using تتطلع.
rows.why: He used شوف (see) for 'look'; Amal: No, we're using تتطلع.

rows.amal_said: You said ما. ... But there's no ما. Why did you put ما؟
rows.why: 'They are looking at you' is not negative; Amal: there's no ما, why did you put ما.
'At you (f)' needs عليكي; he said عليّ (and عليك at 41:12), Amal recast هم بتطلعوا عليكي.

rows.medi_said: أنا، أنا بحب أتطلع على منظرة--
rows.why: He invented a fem form منظرة; Amal supplied منظر and he repeated it.
rows.english: I like to look at the view when I'm in nature.

rows.why: After lamma a state needs akoon; Amal recast أكون في الطبيعة and he asked 'when I be in?' then said لما أكون.

rows.amal_said: اشرحيني is like explain me. اشرحيني. So اشرحيلي is.
rows.why: 'Explain to me' needs -li (la + me), not the object -ni; Amal: اشرحيني is like explain me, so اشرحيلي.
English 'home' inside an Arabic clause; sheet row 'house | Bait | بيت'. Could be the engine. Pre-ruled tier 3 let-pass.
rows.english: Invite them home to your gathering.

rows.amal_said: إم؟ ... شو يعني we worry؟ ... You are worried or you worry؟
rows.why: He blended بنقلق and قلقان; Amal asked 'we worry? You are worried or you worry?' and he said قلقانين.
rows.english: My fiancée and I are worried.

rows.amal_said: عرس، عرس no. بس 300 is more than 10 so. ... so 300 شخص.
rows.why: Over 10 takes a singular noun; Amal: 300 is more than 10, so شخص.
rows.english: More than 300 people at our wedding.

rows.amal_said: عرس، عرس no. ... عرس is wedding. ... عروس is ريناد.
rows.why: He reached for عروستي (my bride) for 'wedding'; Amal separated عرس (wedding) from عروس (bride).

rows.amal_said: عرس no. We never say it this straightforward. ... (Medi: Is it بعد؟) Yes that is best.
rows.why: 'in more than 6 months' needs بعد; Amal said no, not this straightforward, he offered بعد and she said yes.
rows.english: Our wedding is in more than six months.

rows.amal_said: No ستة is no-- less than 10. ... بس ستة is less than 10.
rows.why: 3-10 takes a plural; Amal: ستة is less than 10, and he said shahur.
'We are not ready' needs the plural adjective; Amal: plural, and he said مش جاهزين.
rows.english: My fiancée and I are not ready.

rows.why: After جاهزين (ready to) the next verb drops b-; he said بنصير at 54:59 and again at 56:17, Amal recast نصير at 56:18.
rows.english: We are not ready to become bride and groom.

rows.amal_said: We plan for. ... we plan for it in Arabic.
rows.why: خطط takes لـ; Amal: we plan for, and he said بن... لـ عرس.
rows.english: We are planning for a wedding.

rows.why: Same slip again after her fix at 55:33; Amal prompted لا (la-) and he said بنخطط لـ عرس.
rows.english: We are planning for a wedding.

rows.why: He took بطلب for بطلع; Amal: No, that's بطلع.

rows.medi_said: I'm drawing a blank if you can tell me.
rows.amal_said: So بطلب is to request، ask of، or order.
rows.why: He asked her to tell him the meaning; she supplied it - a didn't-know.
'Request a day off' is a command; Amal: No. Command, and he said اطلبي عطلة.
